_comment: Golden set for the retrieval eval (Task 10). Page numbers are 1-based and refer to
document.pdf in this directory. If that document is ever replaced, EVERY expectedPages
value here must be re-authored -- a stale mapping makes the eval silently meaningless.
The questions deliberately avoid reusing the page headings verbatim, so retrieval has to
match on body content rather than on a title keyword. Several of them target pages 8-11,
which are all eigen-related -- that adjacency is the point: it forces fine discrimination
between semantically close pages, which is the realistic hard case.
OFF-TOPIC SET, WIDENED 2026-08-16. It was three probes, and the measured off-topic ceiling
of 0.641 came from ONE of them -- an instruction-shaped query that is technical and
ordering-flavoured. A ceiling drawn from a single probe cannot bound real chat traffic, so
MIN_SIMILARITY sat 0.009 above a number that had no margin behind it.
The twelve here are chosen to be HARD rather than flattering: instruction-shaped requests
networking) and neighbouring mathematics (calculus, proof) that shares register and
vocabulary with linear algebra without being about it. Plain trivia is kept as a floor
reference. If this narrows or closes the gap, that is the finding -- better discovered here

onTopic.question: What quantity do a matrix's eigenvalues add up to?
What is a matrix called when an eigenvalue's geometric multiplicity is smaller than its algebraic multiplicity?
Which property of a real matrix guarantees it has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors?
Once a matrix is written as P D P inverse, how do you raise it to a large power cheaply?
Which result says a truncated factorization gives the best low-rank approximation?
Why does the classical orthogonalization procedure lose accuracy in floating point, and what is used instead?
What do rank and nullity add up to for a matrix?
Which factorization of a definite matrix costs roughly half of a general LU factorization?
When fitting by minimising squared error, what is the residual vector orthogonal to?
What determines how many blocks an eigenvalue contributes in the canonical form?
